correctness.rationale: With λ(ae+u)=a and β_x(y)=B̃(x,y), the product is λ(x)y+β_x(y)e, where B̃=⟨1⟩⊥B. The commutator of left multiplications is e⊗(λ(x)β_y−λ(y)β_x), since β_x(e)=λ(x). Symmetry of B̃ gives [x,y]=λ(x)y−λ(y)x with λ([x,y])=0, proving the pre-Lie identity over every field. The term λ(x)y stays in any subspace containing x,y; thus closure is equivalent to containing e or having B̃ vanish on every pair in the subspace. These alternatives are disjoint since B̃(e,e)=1. For odd finite fields with nonsingular B, the first family is counted by the Grassmann polynomial of V with degree shifted by one. For an isotropic r-space U the induced quotient U⊥/U has dimension N−2r and determinant class (−1)^r det B. The zero-norm count in this quotient follows from the finite-field quadratic Gauss sum, and double counting one-dimensional extensions gives I_{r+1}=I_r(C_r−1)/(q^{r+1}−1). This includes the nonsplit vanishing case. Odd N has zero counts independent of the determinant; even N has different I_1 for the two signs. The independent direct prime-field closure enumeration reproduced all twelve selected cases and the displayed coefficients.

value.rationale: The family naturally extends a standard small pre-Lie example by a symmetric form. Its closure criterion identifies the entire collection of embedded subalgebras, including nonunital ones, with two explicit families even for degenerate forms and in characteristic two. In odd nonsingular cases it explains structurally why the census can detect the discriminant in one parity and not the other. Value lies in the identification and the field-sensitive interpretation for these pre-Lie algebras, not in independently recounting standard polar subspaces or a second rank-one census.
residual_risks: The polynomial is not an abstract subalgebra-isomorphism count or an automorphism-orbit census. No finite-field enumeration formula for degenerate or characteristic-two forms is claimed.
